opus.reason: Devoted includes loyalty, standing by people when it counts, and adds warmth and attentive affection, so the two differ mainly in emphasis.

sonnet.reason: Both involve lively engagement with work, but enthusiastic is about visible eagerness and gladness, while energetic is about physical vigor and stamina; either can occur without the other.

opus.reason: Both involve visible energy in work, but enthusiasm centres on eager gladness while energetic centres on brisk pace and stamina, and either can occur without the other.

opus.reason: Both involve energy and visible positive emotion, but enthusiasm is eagerness toward tasks while extraversion is broad social outgoingness, assertiveness and excitement-seeking; neither implies the other.

Both involve anxiety about bodily symptoms signalling the end, but hypochondria centers on fearing serious illness and seeking reassurance, while death-fearing centers on dread of mortality and reminders of death; each adds something the other lacks.

opus.reason: Both read bodily twinges as dire signs, but hypochondria centres on fearing illness and seeking reassurance, while death-fearing is a broader dread of mortality, funerals and the grave.

sonnet.reason: Hypochondriac is an anxious fear of illness without real disease, while sickly is actually being frequently ill with a weak constitution; both involve health but are different concepts.

Hypochondria is a specific health-anxiety, while Big Five neuroticism is a broad trait covering worry, irritability, sadness, self-consciousness and stress vulnerability; health worry is only one possible expression, and neuroticism lacks the illness focus.

Both concern attention to one's health, but hypochondria is anxious fear of illness with misread symptoms and reassurance-seeking, while health-consciousness is sensible preventive habits and prompt care; neither implies the other.
Both concern attitude toward one's health, but the hypochondriac is anxiously over-attentive to illness while the health-negligent person ignores it, so they sit at opposite ends of the same quality.

Hypochondriac is a psychological fear of illness despite being well, while healthy is actually having good physical health; they concern the same area (health) but are not reverse ends of one quality, and a hypochondriac may in fact be healthy.

Both involve anxious preoccupation with one's own body, but one is fear of serious illness and the other is concern with weight, shape and appearance, so they are neighbours rather than the same concept.

sonnet.reason: Both involve steady pursuit of a goal, but purposeful stresses having a clear aim that guides choices, while persevering stresses persisting through setbacks and difficulty; neither implies the other.

opus.reason: Both describe steady pursuit of a goal, but purposeful stresses having a clear aim that guides every choice, while persevering stresses persisting through setbacks; each can exist without the other.

Purposeful is about steady goal-directed determination, while wise is about good judgment, foresight and learning from experience; they are neighbours (both involve weighing choices by where they lead) but distinct.

opus.reason: Both centre on steady pursuit of a goal, but Capricorn adds prudence, groundedness and practical competence, while purposeful stresses keeping a clear aim and measuring each choice against it.

sonnet.reason: Both involve honoring commitments and being reliable to others, but steadfast stresses holding firm under cost or pressure, while dependable stresses consistent follow-through without reminders; each adds something the other lacks.

opus.reason: Both mean holding firm to people despite cost, but steadfast also covers commitments generally, while loyal narrows this to allegiance to one's own people and sides.

sonnet.reason: Both involve keeping commitments when it's costly, but trustworthy adds honesty and confidence-keeping while steadfast adds persistence in loyalty to people and unpopular stands.
Both involve holding to principles at a cost, but steadfast is loyalty to commitments and people, while honorable is adherence to a code of absolute moral limits on means; neither implies the other.

Both involve honoring obligations, but steadfast stresses staying loyal and firm under cost or pressure, while responsible stresses diligently carrying out duties and self-reliance; each adds something the other lacks.
